summary: Use HStack for a row of related content. It owns horizontal rhythm, alignment, and optional wrapping while the host decides how much room the row has.

from.quote: Use HStack for a row of related content.

useWhen.text: Related actions and values that belong in one visual row.

from.quote: Keep related actions and values in one visual row.

useWhen.text: Items that belong to one row and should share a rhythm.

from.quote: Use HStack when items belong to one row and should share a rhythm.

useWhen.text: A value, status and action that describe one decision.

from.quote: Pair a value, status, and action when they describe one decision.

avoidWhen.text: Unrelated page sections: use a horizontal stack for related siblings.

from.quote: Use a horizontal stack for related siblings, not unrelated page sections.

anatomy.holds: The children, arranged left to right; reverse changes the visual direction only, and DOM order stays the same.

from.quote: Children are arranged left to right. Reverse changes visual direction only; DOM order stays the same.

anatomy.holds: The Slot gap that sets the row's rhythm, owned by HStack rather than child margins.

from.quote: Use Slot gap to set rhythm. Keep spacing owned by HStack instead of adding child margins.

anatomy.holds: The Figma variant named “Aligment”: Top Left maps to the top edge, and Left centers the row vertically.

from.quote: Figma exposes the variant named “Aligment”: Top Left maps to the top edge and Left centers the row vertically.

anatomy.holds: The inset around the slot: Default supplies it; None when the surrounding owner already supplies that edge.

from.quote: Default supplies the inset around the slot. Use None when the surrounding owner already supplies that edge.

placementAdvice.text: Place the primitive where the relationship happens.

from.quote: Place the primitive where the relationship happens

placementAdvice.text: HStack owns horizontal rhythm, alignment and optional wrapping; the host decides how much room the row has.

from.quote: It owns horizontal rhythm, alignment, and optional wrapping while the host decides how much room the row has.

placementAdvice.text: Populate public component slots with HStack instead of recreating child margins.

from.quote: Populate public component slots with HStack instead of recreating child margins.

placementAdvice.text: Design the host relationship: make the container boundary and content order clear before changing gap or wrap.

from.quote: Make the container boundary and content order clear before changing gap or wrap.

configuration.text: Set the row's rhythm with Slot gap, XS through XL; the gap belongs to the HStack owner.

from.quote: Use XS through XL to set the rhythm of one row. The gap belongs to the HStack owner.

configuration.text: Keep spacing owned by HStack instead of adding child margins.

from.quote: Keep spacing owned by HStack instead of adding child margins.

configuration.text: Use Padding None when the host already owns the edge; Default gives the row its component inset.

from.quote: Default gives the row its component inset. None is useful when the host already owns the edge.

configuration.text: Do not stack component insets without a reason: nested owners can create an unintended double edge and weaken alignment.

from.quote: Nested owners can create an unintended double edge and weaken alignment.

configuration.text: Use wrap inside a constrained width: wrapping needs one.

from.quote: Wrapping needs a constrained width.

configuration.text: Let the available container decide when a wrapped row needs a second line.

from.quote: Let the available container decide when a wrapped row needs a second line.

configuration.text: Do not let the row's children spill out of the owner: a row without a width constraint can overflow and lose its relationship to the parent.

from.quote: A row without a width constraint can overflow and lose its relationship to the parent.

configuration.text: To match Figma's Alignment Left, set alignVertical to center; the default, flex-start, is Figma's Top Left.
Alignment changes the cross-axis position; it never changes row direction.

from.quote: Alignment changes the cross-axis position; it never changes row direction.

configuration.text: Use alignment to support the row, not to replace content hierarchy.

from.quote: Alignment supports the row; it does not replace content hierarchy.

configuration.text: Keep Color Mode and Stack Context consistent with the surrounding public component: HStack and its children inherit the selected Coin mode context.

from.quote: HStack and its children inherit the selected Coin mode context. Keep color mode and stack context consistent with the surrounding public component.

states.when: No mode changes: HStack uses its default direction and token rhythm.

from.quote: uses its default direction and token rhythm.

states.when: A larger Slot gap on the owner: the whole group's rhythm changes.

from.quote: Changing the owner gap changes the whole group.

states.when: Padding None: a containing pattern owns the edge inset.

from.quote: None lets a containing pattern own the edge inset.

states.when: wrap set and the host supplies a width constraint: wrapping appears.

from.quote: Wrapping appears when the host supplies a constraint.

accessibility.text: Keep the children's order meaningful: reverse changes visual order while assistive technology still follows the DOM order.

from.quote: Reverse changes visual order while assistive technology still follows the DOM order.

doDont.do: Wrap inside a real width boundary
doDont.dont: Let children spill out of the owner
doDont.why: A row without a width constraint can overflow and lose its relationship to the parent.

from.quote: Wrap inside a real width boundary

doDont.do: Let the host own the edge inset
doDont.dont: Stack component insets without a reason
doDont.why: Nested owners can create an unintended double edge and weaken alignment.

from.quote: Let the host own the edge inset

examples.purpose: A value, its status and the action for one decision, centered on the cross axis.
examples.jsx:
<HStack alignVertical="center" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }}>
  <Text text="₹2,499" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />
  <Badge label="Due today" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />
  <Button label="Pay" onPress={() => {}} modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />
</HStack>

from.quote: Pair a value, status, and action when they describe one decision.

examples.purpose: A row that wraps inside a bounded width.
examples.jsx:
<HStack wrap style={{ width: 150 }} modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }}>
  <Badge label="Paid" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />
  <Badge label="Due today" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />
  <Badge label="New" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />
</HStack>

from.quote: HStack can wrap when its width is constrained.

examples.purpose: A row with Padding None inside a VStack that owns the edge inset.
examples.jsx:
<VStack modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }}>
  <HStack justifyHorizontal="space-between" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', Padding: 'None' }}>
    <Text text="Amount" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', Padding: 'None' }} />
    <Text text="₹2,499" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', Padding: 'None' }} />
  </HStack>
</VStack>

from.quote: None is useful when the host already owns the edge.

props.name: children
props.description: The content to display inside the stack.

props.name: alignVertical
props.description: Figma's variant is spelled Aligment; Top Left is the default and maps to top alignment, while Left centers the row. Declared: Alignment of children along the cross axis (vertical for HStack). Maps to alignItems. Defaults to `flex-start` (Figma Alignment=Top Left). Pass `center` for Figma Alignment=Left. This is a layout prop, not a Figma variant.

props.name: justifyHorizontal
props.description: Justification of children along the main axis (horizontal for HStack). Maps to justifyContent. Defaults to `flex-start`.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Wrapping needs a constrained width. Declared: Controls whether children can wrap. Maps to flexWrap.

props.name: reverse
props.description: Reverses the visual direction. Declared: If true, reverses the direction of the stack (row-reverse). Default false, from the component source.

props.name: as
props.description: Prop for web semantics, often mapped to HTML tags.

props.name: modes
props.description: Modes object to override default variable values.

props.name: ...ViewProps
props.description: Inherited React Native props the component also accepts. They are not part of the design contract and no guide documents them.
